# Meditate

> Operator-controlled, recoverable consolidation of behavioral directives loaded by Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.

Meditate addresses monotonic instruction append: agents add exception clauses after corrections but rarely replace the obsolete rule. It preserves temporal and source provenance, asks a pinned model for an exact total-disposition plan, validates that plan locally, and archives target bytes before an approved write.

## Canonical documentation

- [Documentation](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/): Overview, workflow, safety model, installation, and command reference
- [Privacy](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/privacy.html): Local processing, provider calls, archives, and telemetry boundaries
- [Source README](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/README.md): Detailed operator guide
- [Design brief](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/docs/design-brief.md): Authority, evidence, transaction, and acceptance contracts
- [Full agent reference](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/llms-full.txt): Expanded machine-readable product reference

## Important boundaries

- `inspect` is local-only and makes no model call.
- `plan` never mutates instruction targets, but it sends current directive text and selected, locally secret-scanned/redacted evidence to the pinned Anthropic model.
- Model output is untrusted and cannot mint paths or durable IDs.
- `apply` requires exact plan-hash approval and archive-before-write.
- Raw histories, auto-memory, and Kindex are read-only evidence.
- Meditate is alpha software and is not a universal agent-state scrubber.
